name: git-code-review
description: Reviews the file you are editing against your own Git Code Review server: credentials, code analysis and the same triage the nightly scan uses.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: The file being edited is sent to the server this is pointed at, so the workspace has to be one you trust.

gitCodeReview.server.markdownDescription: The address of your Git Code Review server, ending in `/api/v1`. It is printed on the **IDE tokens** page of the server itself.

gitCodeReview.token.markdownDescription: Your API token. Better left empty: run **Git Code Review: Set the token** instead and it is kept in the editor's secret storage rather than in a settings file that ends up in backups and sometimes in a repository.

enumDescriptions: When you save, and when you open a file.
As you type, once you stop for a moment.
Only when you ask, with the command.
gitCodeReview.reviewOn.description: When to review. A review runs the engines on the server, which is seconds rather than milliseconds, so 'type' costs the server real work on every pause.

gitCodeReview.changedLinesOnly.description: Show findings only on lines you changed against HEAD. A repository with two thousand findings in it will otherwise show you two thousand findings, and none of them are yours.

gitCodeReview.allowInsecureTls.description: Accept a server certificate this machine does not trust. Off, and worth leaving off: install the certificate authority instead.
